q: Why do reinforcing bars have deformations (lugs) on their surface?
o: To interlock with the concrete and improve bond
To make the bars lighter per metre
To mark the bar grade only
To slow down rusting of the steel
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: The lugs bear against the concrete like small keys, so deformed bars grip far better than plain round bars. That is why codes require deformed bars for main reinforcement.

q: In a tensile test of a steel bar, what is the gage length?
o: The total length of the specimen
The marked length over which elongation is measured
The length held inside the grips
Ten times the bar diameter, always
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Two marks are made on the bar before testing. The change in the distance between them, divided by the original distance, gives the elongation.

q: What is the approximate mass per metre of a 16 mm reinforcing bar?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: A handy formula is mass = d²/162 kg/m with d in mm: 16² / 162 = 256 / 162 = 1.58 kg/m. It comes from steel's density of 7,850 kg/m³. Weighing bars per metre checks that they are not undersized.

q: Under ASTM A615, in which size range is Grade 280 (Grade 40) bar usually made?
o: Only the largest sizes, 36 mm and up
The smaller sizes, about 10 to 19 mm
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: ASTM A615 supplies Grade 280 (40) only in the small sizes, #3 to #6 (about 10 to 19 mm). Larger bars come in Grade 420 (60) and higher.

q: Grade 280 in metric rebar grading is roughly the same as which grade in the English system?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Metric grades give the minimum yield in MPa and English grades in ksi. 280 MPa ≈ 40 ksi, 420 MPa ≈ 60 ksi and 520 MPa ≈ 75 ksi. PNS 49 uses Grade 230, 275 and 415.

q: What is the ultimate tensile strength of a steel bar?
o: The stress at which it first yields
The highest stress it reaches in a tensile test
The stress at which it finally breaks
The stress at its proportional limit
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: It is the peak of the stress-strain curve. For rebar it is well above the yield strength (for example about 620 MPa for Grade 420), which gives reserve strength.

q: What is a reinforcing steel bar?
o: A steel beam used in building frames
A steel sheet used for roofing
A plain or deformed steel bar used in concrete
A steel cable used in bridges
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Rebar is made plain or deformed. Deformed bars are used for almost all structural reinforcement because of their bond; plain bars are used mostly for dowels and spirals.

q: What property is used to name the grade of a reinforcing bar?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Grade 275 means a minimum yield of 275 MPa, Grade 415 a minimum yield of 415 MPa. Designers use the yield strength fy in calculations.

q: Under PNS 49 and ASTM A615, how does the required elongation of a bar depend on its size?
o: Larger bars are allowed a lower minimum elongation
All sizes need the same elongation
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: The standards set a minimum percent elongation that falls a little as bar size increases, because thick bars are harder to stretch uniformly.

q: What does a tensile test of a reinforcing bar measure?
o: Its yield strength, tensile strength and elongation
Its rate of corrosion in seawater
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: The bar is pulled until it breaks. The test gives the yield strength, the ultimate tensile strength and the elongation, which together show strength and ductility.

q: What is a plain bar?
o: A bar rolled with transverse lugs
A bar with an epoxy coating
A round bar with no surface deformations
A bar bent into a hook
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Plain bars bond poorly, so they are used only where bond does not matter much, such as dowels at expansion joints and some spirals.

q: How is the percent elongation of a steel bar computed?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Elongation is the stretch at fracture as a percentage of the original gage length. It measures ductility: how much the bar can stretch before it breaks.

q: When deformed bars are inspected, which feature of the lugs is measured?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: The standard sets a minimum average lug height, average spacing and maximum gap, because these control how well the bar bonds.

q: What does the percent elongation of a bar indicate?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Higher elongation means the bar can stretch a lot before breaking, which gives warning and lets structures absorb earthquake energy.

q: On a deformed bar, what is measured between the transverse lugs?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Lug spacing must not exceed 0.7 times the nominal diameter. If the lugs are too far apart, the bar grips the concrete less.

q: Grade 520 in metric rebar grading is roughly the same as which grade in the English system?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: 520 MPa ≈ 75 ksi. High-strength Grade 520 bars reduce congestion in heavily loaded columns.

q: On a deformed bar, what is the "gap" that is checked?
o: The gap between lug ends on either side of the bar
The space between two bars in a beam
The space between the bar and the formwork
The width of a crack in the concrete
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: The lugs do not wrap all the way around; they stop short of the longitudinal ribs. The total gap is limited (to about 12.5% of the bar perimeter) so enough lug surface grips the concrete.

q: Where should a designer check which rebar grades and sizes are actually available?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Not every grade is rolled in every size in the Philippines. Specifying a size or grade that mills do not make can delay a project, so designers check PNS 49 and supplier stock.

q: Which of these is NOT a standard nominal diameter of reinforcing bar?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Common nominal diameters are 10, 12, 16, 20, 25, 28, 32, 36, 40 and 50 mm. 14 mm is not a standard rebar size.

q: How is the elongation of a steel specimen expressed?
o: As a ratio of bar diameters
As a percentage of the original gage length
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Elongation is a percentage. For example, a 200 mm gage length that becomes 224 mm has stretched 12%.

q: Grade 415 deformed bar under PNS 49 has what minimum yield strength?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Grade numbers give the minimum yield strength in MPa. Grade 415 (about 60 ksi) is the usual grade for main bars in Philippine buildings.

q: Under ASTM A615, in which size range is Grade 520 (Grade 75) bar made?
o: The larger sizes, about 19 mm and up
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: High-strength Grade 520 (75) is rolled in the larger sizes, about #6 to #18 (19 to 57 mm), where it saves the most steel.

q: A bar has an original gage length of 200 mm and a final gage length of 224 mm. What is its elongation?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615

q: Which of these is a standard commercial length of reinforcing bar in the Philippines?
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Bars are commonly sold in 6.0, 7.5, 9.0, 10.5 and 12.0 m lengths. Cutting lists are planned around these to reduce waste.

q: What is a deformed bar?
o: A bar with surface lugs or ribs rolled onto it
A bar that has been bent by mistake
A bar with a smooth surface
ref: PNS 49:2020 Steel bars for concrete reinforcement; ASTM A615
n: Deformed bars are rolled with ribs so they bond with the concrete. They are required for main reinforcement in reinforced concrete.
